rationale: named_funcs is an exact 1.0 rather than a margin below measurement: every `fn` and every trait `fn` signature in the corpus is an entity, including the ten `fn`s nested inside another function's body, so any regression is a real walker bug and not noise. The 2 uncaptured call nodes of 874 are both `(self.call)(self, prestate, haystack, needle)` in memmem/searcher.rs — a call through a function pointer held in a struct field, whose callee parses as a `parenthesized_expression`. There is no name at that call site to resolve against; recovering one needs dataflow, and inventing one would fabricate an edge. MACRO SHARE, measured not assumed: `macro_invocation` is in this language's call set and accounts for 84 of the 874 call nodes here (9.6%), matching the 332 of 3443 (9.6%) over all 63 memchr files. They ARE emitted, which is why `calls` reads 0.998 rather than 0.902. That is defensible only because the edges have targets: `macro_rules!` definitions are extracted as Callables (tagged `macro`), so 73.8% of the macro invocations in this fixture name a macro declared in these very files — 29.8% across the whole repo, where a further 52.7% are std/core constructs (`assert!`, `vec!`, `write!`) that no project Callable can ever satisfy and 17.5% belong to third-party crates. Those two groups resolve to nothing and are dropped silently by resolve_calls, exactly as an unresolved `.unwrap()` is. Closures are excluded from named_funcs by design (ADR-0031): 50 of the 72 closure nodes here produce no entity, and the 136 call nodes inside them attribute upward to the enclosing named function rather than vanishing. No uid collides.
